match.reason: The bank point covers relativistic mass-energy and momentum at far greater depth than the Year 11 VCE topic of momentum, impulse and conservation, so no bank point teaches the same idea at the right depth.

draft.title: Momentum and impulse
card: Momentum is mass times velocity: p = mv. It is measured in kg m/s and has a direction, the same as the velocity.
Impulse is force times the time the force acts: impulse = FΔt. It equals the change in momentum: FΔt = Δp = mv - mu.
For the same change in momentum, a longer contact time means a smaller average force. This is why a crumple zone or a soft landing reduces the force.
In a system with no external force, total momentum stays the same. The momentum before a collision equals the momentum after it.
draft.remember: Impulse equals change in momentum. More time means less force for the same change.

a.q: A 0.50 kg ball moving at 6.0 m/s is caught by a player and brought to rest in 0.20 s. What is the average force on the ball?
a.why: The change in momentum is 0.50 × 6.0 = 3.0 kg m/s. Force = 3.0 ÷ 0.20 = 15 N. The answer 3.0 N is the momentum change, which has not been divided by the time.
a.clue: Find the change in momentum first, then divide by the time.

b.q: Tariq lands from a jump with his knees bent, so he stops over a longer time than with stiff legs. His momentum change is the same both ways. Why is the force on him smaller?
opts: The same impulse is spread over a longer time
The impulse is smaller when the time is longer
His momentum change is smaller with bent knees
The force and the time are not related to impulse
b.why: Impulse FΔt equals the change in momentum, which is the same in both landings. If Δt is larger, F must be smaller. The impulse does not shrink, because it is fixed by the momentum change.
b.clue: The momentum change is fixed, so what must happen to F when Δt grows?

b.best: The same impulse is spread over a longer time

problems.detail: The card writes Δp = mv - mu but never says that u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity. Some students may not know this convention.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly right answer (15 N, and the same impulse spread over a longer time), and the physics checks out. The only issue is minor: the card uses u in mv - mu without defining it as the initial velocity.
